issue.title: SQL: integer parameter validation in string functions (#58923)

labels.name: Team:QL (Deprecated)
labels.description: Meta label for query languages team

repository.name: elasticsearch

issue.body:
Related to #58923

In `insert` function, when argument `start` is larger than `Integer.MAX_INT`, it causes overflow and the number becomes negative. This commit fixed the bug and return origin input when `start` is larger than `Integer.MAX_INT`

According to original code logic about `insert` function `insert(input, start, length, replaceString)`:
1. when the argument `start` is larger than length of `input`, it should return origin `input`;
2. when the argument `start` is less or equal than `0`, it should work as `insert(input, 1, length, replaceString)`.

In original code, when the `start` is larger than `Integer.MAX_INT`, it causes overflow and the start becomes negative. This triggers the second situation above, and the function works as `insert(input, 1, length, replaceString)`. However, this expects to return origin `input`.

body: There's one more discrepancy that'd be worth addressing with the string functions: some will only accept an integer parameter (like [`SUBSTRING`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bc82b93f467ba5ce22f4b5b71b129bb49acda58b/x-pack/plugin/sql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/sql/expression/function/scalar/string/Substring.java#L56)), while others will accept floating points too (like [`INSERT`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bc82b93f467ba5ce22f4b5b71b129bb49acda58b/x-pack/plugin/sql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/sql/expression/function/scalar/string/Insert.java#L58)).

issue.body:
Related to #58923

In insert, locate, substring function, when argument `start` or `length` is greater than Integer.MAX_INT OR less then Integer.MIN_INT + 1 (note that `start` needs to minus 1), it causes overflow and leads to unexpected results.

body: @bpintea Yes, the parameter type was different from `insert`, `locate` and `substring`. But in *FunctionProcessor, the integer or rational parameters of these functions are all cast into integer, hence they can treat as integer to check integer overflow.

issue.body:
This PR adds integer parameter validation for the string functions taking one: LOCATE, LEFT, INSERT, REPEAT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING.

Closes #58923.
Supersedes #60281.
